Human fertilization is the union of a human egg and sperm.
Human fertilization usually occurs in the ampulla of the fallopian tube.
The result of the union of a human egg and sperm is a zygote cell, also called a fertilized egg.
The union of a human egg and sperm initiates prenatal development.
Scientists discovered the dynamics of human fertilization in the nineteenth century.
The process of fertilization involves a sperm fusing with an ovum.
The most common sequence of fertilization begins with ejaculation during copulation.
The most common sequence of fertilization is followed by ovulation.
The most common sequence of fertilization finishes with fertilization.
Various exceptions to the most common sequence of fertilization are possible.
One exception to the sequence of fertilization is artificial insemination.
One exception to the sequence of fertilization is in vitro fertilization.
One exception to the sequence of fertilization is external ejaculation without copulation.
One exception to the sequence of fertilization is copulation shortly after ovulation.
Upon encountering the secondary oocyte, the acrosome of the sperm produces enzymes.
The enzymes from the acrosome of the sperm allow the sperm to burrow through the outer jelly coat of the egg.
The sperm plasma fuses with the egg's plasma membrane.
The sperm head disconnects from its flagellum.
The egg travels down the Fallopian tube to reach the uterus.

The table columns are No., Cloverway Inc. title, original Japanese and Viz Media titles, episode director(s), writer(s), art director(s), animation director(s), original airdate, and English airdate in the United States.

Episode 90 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Star Struck, Bad Luck', the Viz Media title 'Premonition of the Apocalypse: The Mysterious New Guardians Appear', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Chikyū hōkai no yokan? Nazo no shin Senshi shutsugen'.

Episode 90 was directed by Junichi Sato, written by Sukehiro Tomita, art directed by Kenichi Tajiri, and animation directed by Masahiro Andō. It originally aired on March 19, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on June 12, 2000.
After experiencing apocalyptic visions, Rei is attacked by a powerful monster called a Daimon.
Sailor Moon is unable to fight the Daimon after it disables her brooch, which reverses her transformation.
The Daimon is defeated by a pair of mysterious new warriors.
The girls despondently realize that a new conflict has begun.

Episode 91 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Crystal Clear Again', the Viz Media title 'The Rod of Love Is Born: Usagi's New Transformation', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Ai no roddo tanjō! Usagi no shin henshin'.

Episode 91 was directed by Yūji Endō, written by Shigeru Yanagawa, art directed by Yoshiyuki Shikano, and animation directed by Katsumi Tamegai. It originally aired on March 26, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on June 13, 2000.
While Mamoru strives to cheer Usagi up after her failure in the previous battle, a young girl is the latest target of the Death Busters.
Due to Usagi's inability to transform, the under-powered Sailor Team struggles to fight off the Daimon and is once again forced to rely on the mysterious two warriors.
Once the Sailor Team determines the girl's pure heart is not a talisman, they leave the Sailor Team to fend for themselves.
Tuxedo Mask and Usagi hold hands after the latter's refusal to escape.
Through the power of their love, Usagi's disabled Crystal Star brooch transforms into the Cosmic Heart Compact.
Usagi gains the Spiral Heart Moon Rod and, along with it, the ability to transform and defeat the new enemy.

Episode 92 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Driving Dangerously', the Viz Media title 'A Handsome Boy? Haruka Tenoh's Secret', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Suteki na bishōnen? Ten'ō Haruka no himitsu'.

Episode 92 was directed by Kunihiko Ikuhara, written by Katsuyuki Sumisawa, art directed by Kazuhisa Asai, and animation directed by Hisashi Kagawa. It originally aired on April 16, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on June 14, 2000.
Avoiding their study group, Usagi and Minako meet Haruka Tenou, an attractive and supposedly male student of a prestigious local school.
Usagi and Minako both become infatuated with Haruka.
After Minako is defeated in a racing game, Michiru arrives to pick up Haruka.
Michiru and Haruka depart, with Usagi and Minako following behind them soon after.
Once Michiru and Haruka separate at a mechanic's shop, Usagi and Minako take this as their chance.
Haruka tells Usagi and Minako about 'him'-self until a Daimon arrives to attack Kameda, the shop mechanic.
The Daimon starts to escape when Usagi and Minako transform into their Guardian forms to chase it down.
Uranus and Neptune arrive to investigate Kameda's pure heart crystal.
When the crystal turns out not to be a talisman, Uranus and Neptune retreat.
Sailor Moon defeats the Daimon.
Later, the rest of the girls are at Crown Game Center with Usagi and Minako in hopes of seeing the cute boy they had told them about.
Michiru arrives with a blonde girl, whom Usagi and Minako initially fail to realize is Haruka.
Once Usagi and Minako realize the blonde girl is Haruka, Minako falls to the ground in anguish.
Haruka notes that she had never said she was male.

Episode 93 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Bad Harmony', the Viz Media title 'Usagi's Idol: The Graceful Genius Michiru', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Usagi no akogare! Yūbi no tensai Michiru'.

Episode 93 was directed by Hiroki Shibata, written by Megumi Sugihara, art directed by Kazuyuki Hashimoto, and animation directed by Taichi Nakamura. It originally aired on April 23, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on June 15, 2000.
When Usagi is concerned that she is not smart enough to be with Mamoru after being scolded by the other girls, she seeks advice from Michiru Kaioh.
Michiru Kaioh suggests that Usagi and Mamoru go to a violin recital.

Episode 94 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Swept Off Her Feet', the Viz Media title 'Protect the Pure Heart: The Three-Way Battle', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Pyua na kokoro wo mamore! Teki mikata mittsu tomoe ransen'.

Episode 94 was directed by Noriyo Sasaki, written by Sukehiro Tomita, art directed by Kenichi Tajiri, and animation directed by Ikuko Itō. It originally aired on April 30, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on June 16, 2000.
Usagi's friend, Unazuki, is attacked by a Daimon and has her pure heart crystal stolen.
When Sailor Moon tries to take the crystal back to Unazuki, Uranus and Neptune attempt to steal it in order to claim the Talisman.

Episode 95 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Blinded By Love's Light', the Viz Media title 'Let Moon Help With Your Love Problems', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Koi no otasuke wa Mūn ni omakase'.

Episode 95 was directed by Harume Kosaka, written by Shigeru Yanagawa, art directed by Yoshiyuki Shikano, and animation directed by Mari Tominaga. It originally aired on May 7, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on June 19, 2000.
Naru and Umino enter an affection contest in order to prove their strong mutual romantic love for each other.
Naru and Umino find themselves targeted by a Daimon.

Episode 96 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Lita Borrows Trouble', the Viz Media title 'Coldhearted Uranus: Makoto in Danger', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Reikoku na Uranusu? Makoto no pinchi'.

Episode 96 was directed by Kōnosuke Uda, written by Yoji Enokido, art directed by Kazuhisa Asai, and animation directed by Masahiro Andō. It originally aired on May 14, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on June 20, 2000.
Makoto is targeted by a Daimon, but manages to temporarily evade it.
Haruka wants to analyze Makoto's pure heart crystal, and befriends Makoto in order to get close to her.
Episode 97 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Damp Spirits', the Viz Media title 'The Labyrinth of Water: Ami Targeted', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Mizu no rabarinsu! Nerawareta Ami'.

Episode 97 was directed by Junichi Sato, written by Megumi Sugihara, art directed by Kazuyuki Hashimoto, and animation directed by Katsumi Tamegai. It originally aired on May 21, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on June 21, 2000.
Ami's desire to avoid competition leads her to inadvertently offend Michiru in a swimming race.
Usagi accidentally hurts Ami's feelings.
Meanwhile, a Daimon selects Ami as a target.

Episode 98 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Friendly Foes', the Viz Media title 'To Save Our Friends: Moon and Uranus Join Forces', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Tomodachi wo sukue! Mūn Uranusu rengō'.

Episode 98 was directed by Yūji Endō, written by Sukehiro Tomita, art directed by Kenichi Tajiri, and animation directed by Taichi Nakamura. It originally aired on May 28, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on June 22, 2000.
After Sailor Neptune is captured and possibly killed by Kaolinite, Sailor Moon and Sailor Uranus find themselves shackled together.
Sailor Moon and Sailor Uranus are forced to reassess their less-than-friendly attitudes toward each other in order to save Sailor Neptune from further harm.

Episode 99 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Mixed Emotions', the Viz Media title 'A Man's Kindness: Yuichiro Heartbroken by Rei', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Otoko no yasashisa! Yūichirō Rei ni shitsuren?'.

Episode 99 was directed by Harume Kosaka, written by Megumi Sugihara, art directed by Yoshiyuki Shikano, and animation directed by Shinya Hasegawa. It originally aired on June 18, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on June 23, 2000.
Worried by Rei's intensive meditation, Yuuichirou becomes concerned that she has fallen deeply head-over-heels in love for another man.
When Yuuichirou sees Rei with Haruka and mistakes Haruka for a man, he is convinced that 'he' is Rei's new romantic suitor.

Episode 100 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Individual Happiness', the Viz Media title 'I Want to Quit Being a Sailor Guardian: Minako's Dilemma', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Sērā Senshi wo yametai!? Minako no nayami'.

Episode 100 was directed by Hiroki Shibata, written by Yoji Enokido, art directed by Kazuhisa Asai, and animation directed by Mari Tominaga. It originally aired on June 25, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on June 26, 2000.
Minako is despondent about her double life of being a Sailor Guardian and a normal girl.
Meanwhile, an old friend of Minako's, who she once fell in love with, is attacked by a Daimon.
Minako, as Sailor Venus, must use her skills of volleyball to save the old friend.

Episode 101 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Birthday Blues, Part 1', the Viz Media title 'Usagi in Tears: a Glass Slipper for My Birthday', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Usagi namida! Tanjōbi ni garasu no kutsu wo'.

Episode 101 was directed by Yūji Endō, written by Katsuyuki Sumisawa, art directed by Kazuyuki Hashimoto, and animation directed by Masahiro Andō. It originally aired on July 2, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on June 27, 2000.
Usagi is furious when Mamoru forgets her 15th birthday.
When Mamoru buys her an expensive pair of glass slippers to make up for it, he fails to realize that Kaolinite sabotaged the shoes with a Daimon egg to steal her pure heart crystal.
Kaolinite steals Usagi's Cosmic Heart Compact, leaving her unable to transform.
Tuxedo Mask gets captured.

Episode 102 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Birthday Blues, Part Two', the Viz Media title 'The Stolen Pure Heart: Usagi's Crisis', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Ubawareta pyua na kokoro! Usagi zettai zetsumei'.

Episode 102 was directed by Noriyo Sasaki, written by Katsuyuki Sumisawa, art directed by Kenichi Tajiri, and animation directed by Taichi Nakamura. It originally aired on July 16, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on June 28, 2000.
With the Cosmic Heart Compact stolen and Tuxedo Mask kidnapped, Usagi and the four other Sailor Guardians, along with Sailors Uranus and Neptune, go to retake the compact.
They go to retake the compact so Usagi can become Sailor Moon again and rescue Tuxedo Mask.
They face Kaolinite in a final showdown at Tokyo Tower.

Episode 103 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Hello, Sailor Mini Moon', the Viz Media title 'The Arrival of a Tiny Pretty Guardian', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Yatte kita chiccha na Bishōjo Senshi'.

Episode 103 was directed by Kunihiko Ikuhara, written by Shigeru Yanagawa, art directed by Yoshiyuki Shikano, and animation directed by Kazuya Kuroda. It originally aired on August 6, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on June 29, 2000.
Eudial and the Witches 5 are tasked to take over from Kaolinite's position.
The Witches 5 target a genius drummer recruited to play at a festival for Rei.
The Sailor Guardians cannot defeat the Daimon who attacks the drummer.
Chibiusa arrives as the Guardians' newest ally, Sailor Chibi-Moon.

Episode 104 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Tainted Tea Party', the Viz Media title 'Making New Friends: Chibi Moon's Adventure', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Tomodachi wo motomete! Chibi Mūn no katsuyaku'.

Episode 104 was directed by Junichi Sato, written by Megumi Sugihara, art directed by Kazuhisa Asai, and animation directed by Ikuko Itō. It originally aired on August 20, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on June 30, 2000.
Chibiusa has returned from Crystal Tokyo for further training.
Chibiusa attempts to adapt to her new home by making friends her age.
Chibiusa tries to befriend a master who does tea ceremonies, only to become the Death Busters' latest target.

Episode 105 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'People Who Need People', the Viz Media title 'I Want Power: Mako Lost in Doubt', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Pawā ga hoshī! Mako-chan no mayoi michi'.

Episode 105 was directed by Hiroki Shibata, written by Shigeru Yanagawa, art directed by Yoshiyuki Shikano, and animation directed by Mari Tominaga. It originally aired on August 27, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 3, 2000.
Makoto is training in the mountains, trying to become much stronger after being easily defeated by a Daimon before.
Makoto's trainer is attacked, and tells her that nobody can live alone.
Makoto attacks the Daimon and fails, and realizes she needs her best friends in order to win.

Episode 106 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Related By Destiny', the Viz Media title 'The Bond of Destiny: Uranus's Distant Past', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Unmei no kizuna! Uranusu no tōi hi'.

Episode 106 was directed by Takuya Igarashi, written by Yoji Enokido, art directed by Kenichi Tajiri, and animation directed by Katsumi Tamegai. It originally aired on September 3, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 4, 2000.
Haruka remembers the past when she first met Michiru, who told her that she was destined to become Sailor Uranus.
Haruka initially refused that destiny, for she loved her life too much and was afraid of change.
Haruka was attacked, and Sailor Neptune was injured while defending her.
In her anguish, Haruka took the transformation pen and accepted her destiny as Sailor Uranus, the Sailor Guardian of the Sky.

Episode 107 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Art Appreciation', the Viz Media title 'Art Is an Explosion of Love: Chibiusa's First Love', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Geijutsu wa ai no bakuhatsu! Chibiusa no hatsukoi'.

Episode 107 was directed by Yūji Endō, written by Katsuyuki Sumisawa, art directed by Minoru Ōkōchi, and animation directed by Taichi Nakamura. It originally aired on September 10, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 5, 2000.
Chibiusa meets a boy named Masanori at her art class and develops a crush on him.
Masanori already has a crush on Michiru, who is taking a class at that school as well.
When a Daimon attacks Masanori, Chibiusa must take a stand to protect him.

Episode 108 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Everything's Coming Up Rosey', the Viz Media title 'Usagi Dancing to the Waltz', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Usagi no dansu wa warutsu ni notte'.

Episode 108 was directed by Harume Kosaka, written by Megumi Sugihara, art directed by Kazuhisa Asai, and animation directed by Masahiro Andō. It originally aired on September 17, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 6, 2000.
An English gentleman named Edwards invites Mamoru and the girls to a fancy party.
At the party, Usagi accidentally becomes drunk.
At the party, the team is forced to confront a fashionable Eudial and her latest Daimon.

Episode 109 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'No Turning Back', the Viz Media title 'The Shocking Moment: Everyone's Identities Revealed', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Shōgeki no toki! Akasareta tagai no shōtai'.

Episode 109 was directed by Junichi Sato, written by Sukehiro Tomita, art directed by Yoshiyuki Shikano, and animation directed by Kazuya Kuroda. It originally aired on September 24, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 7, 2000.
Minako becomes jealous that a Daimon has not yet attacked her, and she fears that she does not have a pure heart.
After doing as many 'pure' things as she can, Minako is attacked, and her pure heart is taken from her.
When Eudial nearly gets away, Usagi is forced to reveal her identity to Haruka and Michiru.
Haruka and Michiru reveal their identities as Sailors Uranus and Neptune to Sailor Moon.

Episode 110 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Destiny's Arrival', the Viz Media title 'The Death of Uranus and Neptune: The Talisman Appear', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Uranusu-tachi no shi? Tarisuman shutsugen'.

Episode 110 was directed by Kunihiko Ikuhara, written by Yoji Enokido, art directed by Kenichi Tajiri, and animation directed by Mari Tominaga. It originally aired on October 15, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 10, 2000.
Faced with losing her position at Witches 5, Eudial creates a computer program to find the true owners of the three Talismans.
Eudial learns that Haruka and Michiru are the ones who hold two of the Talismans within their own hearts.
Eudial and her companions take away Usagi's brooch, and follow Eudial onto a lonely island.
The invitation turns out to be a trick, and Michiru's pure heart is taken, which turns into the mystical Deep Aqua Mirror.
Haruka, in order to release her own talisman, shoots herself with Eudial's gun.
Haruka's pure heart transforms into the mystical Space Sword.

Episode 111 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'The Purity Chalice', the Viz Media title 'The Holy Grail's Mystical Power: Moon's Double Transformation', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Seihai no shinpi na chikara! Mūn nidan henshin'.

Episode 111 was directed by Hiroki Shibata, written by Sukehiro Tomita, art directed by Kazuyuki Hashimoto, and animation directed by Ikuko Itō. It originally aired on October 22, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 11, 2000.
Sailor Pluto appears and reawakens Sailors Uranus and Neptune.
The three talismans resonate with each other, the third and last being Sailor Pluto's Garnet Orb.
The Holy Grail appears, and Sailor Moon grabs it and evolves into Super Sailor Moon.
Super Sailor Moon drives Eudial out.
Mimete kills Eudial by sabotaging her car with snails.

Episode 112 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Show Stoppers', the Viz Media title 'Who is the True Messiah? Chaos of Light and Darkness', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Shin no kyūseishu wa dare? Hikari to kage no kaosu'.

Episode 112 was directed by Noriyo Sasaki, written by Shigeru Yanagawa, art directed by Minoru Ōkōchi, and animation directed by Shinya Hasegawa. It originally aired on November 5, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 12, 2000.
The girls end up watching the filming of a movie, where Chibiusa encounters Hotaru, whom she quickly befriends.
In the end, Chibiusa is revealed to be the 12-year-old daughter of Professor Souichi Tomoe, the possessed leader of the Death Busters.
Super Sailor Moon uses her new 'Rainbow Moon Heartache' attack to defeat the Daimon of the day.

Episode 113 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Rini's Risky Friendship', the Viz Media title 'A House Filled With Evil Presence: The Beautiful Hotaru's Secret', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Yōki tadayou ie! Bishōjo Hotaru no himitsu'.

Episode 113 was directed by Kōnosuke Uda, written by Megumi Sugihara, art directed by Kenichi Tajiri, and animation directed by Taichi Nakamura. It originally aired on November 12, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 13, 2000.
The three Outer Guardians appear to Tuxedo Mask, and tell him why they cannot fight alongside Sailor Moon and the other four Sailor Guardians.
Usagi and Chibiusa visit Hotaru, and see a woman who looks like Kaolinite.
The Messiah of Silence appears demanding pure hearts.
Episode 114 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Mimet's Mess', the Viz Media title 'I Love Idols: Mimete's Dilemma', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Aidoru daisuki! Nayameru Mimetto'.

Episode 114 was directed by Harume Kosaka, written by Yoji Enokido, art directed by Yoshiyuki Shikano, and animation directed by Masahiro Andō. It originally aired on November 19, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 14, 2000.
Minako and Mimete enter a beauty contest at the same time, with Mimete willing to risk it all to obtain victory.
Both Minako and Mimete fall short of the needed votes to win the idol position.
Mimete decides to go back to her evil ways.

Episode 115 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'The Shadow of Silence', the Viz Media title 'Shadow of Silence: The Pale Glimmer of a Firefly', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Chinmoku no kage!? Awaki Hotaru hi no yurameki'.

Episode 115 was directed by Takuya Igarashi, written by Yoji Enokido, art directed by Kenichi Tajiri, and animation directed by Katsumi Tamegai. It originally aired on November 26, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 17, 2000.
Hotaru overexerts herself and is hospitalized, during which her past without friends is shown, and the reasons for it.
Meanwhile, Mimete targets a soap opera actor.
During the attack on the actor, the attacking Daimon runs near Hotaru, who glows and completely freezes the Daimon.

Episode 116 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Thorny Weather', the Viz Media title 'Sunny Skies After a Storm: A Friendship Dedicated to Hotaru', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Arashi nochi hare! Hotaru ni sasageru yūjō'.

Episode 116 was directed by Yūji Endō, written by Megumi Sugihara, art directed by Kazuhisa Asai, and animation directed by Jouji Yanase. It originally aired on December 3, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 18, 2000.
Mamoru takes Usagi, Chibiusa and Hotaru to a botanical garden that is tended by Yoshiki Kurebayashi, an old classmate of Mamoru's.
While there, Mimete targets Yoshiki's pure heart and causes a storm that puts the plants at risk.
Sailor Moon defeats the accompanying Daimon, U-Bara.

Episode 117 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Heightened Hazard', the Viz Media title 'Higher and Stronger: A Cheer from Usagi', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Yori takaku yori tsuyoku! Usagi no ōen'.

Episode 117 was directed by Kunihiko Ikuhara, written by Shigeru Yanagawa, art directed by Minoru Ōkōchi, and animation directed by Taichi Nakamura. It originally aired on December 10, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 19, 2000.
Hotaru wishes to give a letter to Shun Hayase, a famous athlete.
Shun Hayase becomes targeted when Hotaru goes to give the letter to him.
Hotaru possessively blasts the enemy with a hugely strong amount of energy.
Hotaru talks to Shun about being frail and weak, and he thanks her for talking to him.

Episode 118 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'It's In The Cards', the Viz Media title 'The Battle Inside the Demonic Space: The Sailor Guardians' Gamble', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Makū no tatakai! Sērā Senshi no kake'.

Episode 118 was directed by Noriyo Sasaki, written by Katsuyuki Sumisawa, art directed by Kenichi Tajiri, and animation directed by Masahide Yanagisawa. It originally aired on December 17, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 20, 2000.
Mimete attempts to create a Daimon by herself, throwing the entire Tomoe house into another dimension.
The Guardians enter the dimension and are defeated by a game-master Daimon named U-Ikasaman.
Hotaru manages to assist in U-Ikasaman's defeat by the use of a bluff.

Episode 119 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Goodness Eclipsed', the Viz Media title 'The Messiah of Silence Awakens? Stars of Destiny', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Chinmoku no Meshia kakusei? Unmei no hoshiboshi'.

Episode 119 was directed by Harume Kosaka, written by Yoji Enokido, art directed by Kazuhisa Asai, and animation directed by Shinya Hasegawa. It originally aired on December 24, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on September 13, 2000.
The Sailor Guardians visit a planetarium, where a man is attacked by a Daimon.
The symbol of Saturn appears on Hotaru's forehead, and she attacks the Daimon.
Sailor Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto attack Hotaru, since she is both Sailor Saturn, the Sailor Guardian of Silence, Ruin and Birth, and also possessed by the Messiah of Silence.
Super Sailor Moon takes the blow to protect Hotaru.

Episode 120 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Next In Line', the Viz Media title 'An Invasion from an Another Dimension: Mystery of Infinity Academy', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Ijigen kara no shinryaku! Mugen Gakuen no nazo'.

Episode 120 was directed by Kōnosuke Uda, written by Megumi Sugihara, art directed by Minoru Ōkōchi, and animation directed by Katsumi Tamegai. It originally aired on January 7, 1995 and aired in English in the United States on July 21, 2000.
Chibiusa goes to Hotaru's house to find that Hotaru has disappeared, and is devastated about it.
At the same time, the Sailor Guardians investigate Infinity Academy.
Mimete tries one final time to defeat the Sailor Guardians before Tellu literally pulls the plug on her operation.

Episode 121 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Fiendish Ferns', the Viz Media title 'A Bewitching Flower That Steals Hearts: Tellu, the Third Witch', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Kokoro wo ubau yōka! Daisan no majō Teruru'.

Episode 121 was directed by Takuya Igarashi, written by Shigeru Yanagawa, art directed by Kazuyuki Hashimoto, and animation directed by Taichi Nakamura. It originally aired on January 14, 1995 and aired in English in the United States on July 24, 2000.
Tellu develops a new plan to steal pure hearts, using a plant bred for that purpose.
Setsuna realizes the plant is an alien plant made to steal pure hearts, and warns the Sailor Guardians.
Tuxedo Mask causes a mutated plant to destroy Tellu.
This leads the Sailor Guardians to trace Tellu back to the mysterious Infinity Academy.

Episode 122 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'The Science Of Love', the Viz Media title 'Believe in Love: Ami, the Kindhearted Guardian', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Ai wo shinjite! Ami, kokoro yasashiki Senshi'.

Episode 122 was directed by Yūji Endō, written by Sukehiro Tomita, art directed by Kenichi Tajiri, and animation directed by Hideyuki Motohashi. It originally aired on January 21, 1995 and aired in English in the United States on July 25, 2000.
Ami investigates the Infinity Academy, where she meets Viluy, the fourth of the Witches 5.
Viluy attempts to use her nanorobots to steal pure hearts from entrance exam takers.
After Viluy's battle, her own microscopic robots turn against her, destroying her in the process.

Episode 123 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Wake Up Call', the Viz Media title 'Shadows of Destruction: the Messiah of Silence Awakens', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Hametsu no kage! Chinmoku no Meshia no mezame'.

Episode 123 was directed by Harume Kosaka, written by Megumi Sugihara, art directed by Minoru Ōkōchi, and animation directed by Mari Tominaga. It originally aired on January 28, 1995 and aired in English in the United States on July 26, 2000.
Cyprine is the last of the Witches 5.
Cyprine steals pure hearts from Infinity Academy students.
The Sailor Guardians engage Cyprine, and her alter-ego, Ptilol, in a showdown.
Chibiusa is abducted by the recently resurrected Kaolinite.
Chibiusa's pure heart is stolen by Mistress 9, who has taken over Hotaru's body, which allows her to awaken as the Messiah of Silence.

Episode 124 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Who's Really Who?', the Viz Media title 'The Coming Terror of Darkness: Struggle of the Eight Guardians', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Semari kuru yami no kyōfu! Kusen no Hassenshi'.

Episode 124 was directed by Takuya Igarashi, written by Yoji Enokido, art directed by Kazuyuki Hashimoto, and animation directed by Ikuko Itō. It originally aired on February 4, 1995 and aired in English in the United States on July 28, 2000.
Mistress 9 uses all remaining Daimon eggs to create a powerful energized shield of evil minions around Infinity Academy.
Sailor Moon is abducted, as she is the holder of the Holy Grail.
After witnessing Sailor Pluto ultimately sacrificing herself to save them by using her forbidden ability to stop time, Sailor Uranus and Sailor Neptune destroy Germatoid.
Germatoid is the Daimon possessing Professor Souichi Tomoe.
Sailor Uranus and Sailor Neptune destroy Germatoid with their talismans, the Deep Aqua Mirror and the Space Sword.

Episode 125 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Darkness, My Old Friend', the Viz Media title 'The Shining Shooting Star: Saturn and the Messiah', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Kagayaku ryūsei! Satān soshite kyūseishu'.

Episode 125 was directed by Kōnosuke Uda, written by Yoji Enokido, art directed by Kenichi Tajiri, and animation directed by Ikuko Itō. It originally aired on February 11, 1995 and aired in English in the United States on July 29, 2000.
Sailor Moon is tricked into giving Mistress 9 the Holy Grail, which she uses to summon Pharaoh 90 to Earth.
Hotaru regains consciousness with the assistance of Sailor Moon and her father, destroying Mistress 9.
Hotaru fully awakens the spirit of Sailor Saturn within herself at last.
Sailor Saturn returns Chibiusa's pure heart crystal.
Sailor Saturn appears before Sailor Moon to ultimately sacrifice herself and destroy Pharaoh 90 once and for all with her destructive powers.
Sailor Moon gains the help of the other six Sailor Guardians to become Super Sailor Moon once more.
Super Sailor Moon saves both Hotaru and Sailor Saturn.
Sailor Saturn is reborn as a baby immediately afterward.

Episode 126 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Second Chance', the Viz Media title 'A New Life: Parting of the Stars of Destiny', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Atarashiki seimei! Unmei no hoshiboshi betsuri no toki'.

Episode 126 was directed by Yūji Endō, written by Megumi Sugihara, art directed by Kazuhisa Asai, and animation directed by Taichi Nakamura. It originally aired on February 18, 1995 and aired in English in the United States on July 30, 2000.
Haruka and Michiru give the newly reborn infant Hotaru to a still-healing Professor Souichi Tomoe, who is finally free of the Death Busters.
Haruka and Michiru viciously attack Sailor Moon, for she protected Hotaru's body and Sailor Saturn, and risked the whole entire world for one mere life.
The Silver Crystal throws Haruka and Michiru back.
Haruka and Michiru kneel to Sailor Moon as their leader and leave the city.

Episode 127 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Tough Kindness', the Viz Media title 'A Guardian's Realization: Strength Lies Within a Pure Heart', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Senshi no Jikaku! Tsuyosa wa Pyua na Kokoro no Naka ni'.
Episode 127 was directed by Harume Kosaka and written by Sukehiro Tomita. It originally aired on February 25, 1995 and aired in English in the United States on August 1, 2000.
Chibiusa returns to the future after receiving a letter from her mother, Neo-Queen Serenity.
Meanwhile, a final Daimon emerges from the rubble of Infinity Academy.
Chibiusa returns just in time to help defeat the final Daimon.
A board of directors is a recognized group of people.
A board of directors jointly oversees the activities of an organization.
An organization overseen by a board of directors can be a for-profit business, a nonprofit organization, or a government agency.
A board's powers, duties, and responsibilities are determined by government regulations, including the jurisdiction's corporations law.
A board's powers, duties, and responsibilities are determined by the organization's own constitution and bylaws.
The authorities over a board may specify the number of members of the board.
The authorities over a board may specify how board members are chosen.
The authorities over a board may specify how often the board is to meet.

The Livesey Hall War Memorial commemorates the fallen of World War II.

A transfer case is a part of the drivetrain of four-wheel-drive, all-wheel-drive, and other multiple powered axle vehicles.
A transfer case transfers power from the transmission to the front and rear axles by means of drive shafts.
A transfer case synchronizes the difference between the rotation of the front and rear wheels.
A transfer case may contain one or more sets of low range gears for off-road use.
